observations.source_locator: Printed p. 92, Table II, patient 4; total oxygen-consumption column.
limitations: This is one source-numbered case from Table II, not a group mean or normative value; Table II lists eight oxygen-uptake values among 12 retained patients.

The authors state that umbilical flow and especially oxygen saturation and fetal oxygen consumption are approximate because vessel spasm complicated measurements; they are not true basal-state in-utero values (printed p. 95).
The study involved therapeutic-abortion hysterotomy, anesthesia and surgical manipulation; extrapolation to an undisturbed pregnancy or device requirement is unsupported.
The article reports 32 patients entered, 20 deleted and 12 retained; patient numbers are source-local labels and do not establish any cross-study identity.

limitations: This is a small historical surgical cohort in pregnancies undergoing therapeutic-abortion hysterotomy, not an undisturbed-pregnancy reference cohort.
The authors describe umbilical flow and especially oxygen saturation and fetal oxygen consumption as approximate due to vessel spasm; they state these are not true basal-state in-utero values.
Only 8 of 12 retained Table II rows have uptake values; the blank reason is not reported for the other four.
Values are source-numbered individual cases with rounding and no uncertainty estimates, not gestational-age group means or validated ranges.
Reuse rights for the scanned journal pages were not confirmed; Internet Archive provides public reading access only.
No evidence here defines a healthy fetal oxygen margin, critical delivery threshold or device specification.
